title: Choosing the Right Monetization Model
description: Practice selecting and evaluating monetization models using real-world business scenarios and metrics.

interactions.prompt: A B2B analytics tool shows: 40% of free users hit the usage cap weekly, paid conversion is 2.1%, and churned paid users cite 'not enough value beyond free tier.' What's the key signal?

options.text: The free tier is too generous, cannibalizing paid conversions
The usage cap needs to be raised for free users
Paid tier doesn't deliver enough differentiated value
The product needs more marketing to drive conversions

chartData.title: Free Tier vs Paid Conversion Metrics

interactions.prompt: In a usage-based model like AWS or Twilio, revenue scales with customer ____, aligning the vendor's incentive with the customer's growth.

options.text: consumption
headcount
satisfaction
retention

interactions.prompt: You're launching a project management tool for SMBs. You can either offer a freemium model with a generous free tier to maximize adoption, or a low-cost subscription from day one to validate willingness to pay. Budget supports only one approach.

options.text: Freemium—build a large user base and convert later
Low-cost subscription—validate paying demand early
Usage-based pricing tied to number of projects
Free trial only with 14-day expiration

interactions.prompt: A marketplace like Etsy reports: GMV up 25% YoY, but take rate dropped from 6.5% to 5.2% due to seller fee promotions. Net revenue grew only 8%. What matters most?

options.text: GMV growth proves the marketplace is healthy
Take rate compression is eroding revenue growth despite volume gains
Seller promotions should be increased to drive more GMV
The marketplace should switch to a subscription model for sellers

chartData.title: Marketplace Metrics: Previous Year vs Current Year

interactions.prompt: A SaaS startup is evaluating monetization models. Rank these factors from most to least important when choosing between subscription vs. usage-based pricing.

options.text: Predictability of revenue for fundraising and planning
How variable customer usage patterns are
Competitor pricing structures in the market
Ease of implementation for the billing system

interactions.prompt: Your developer tools company (like Datadog) sees enterprise clients requesting annual contracts with committed spend, while startups prefer pure pay-as-you-go. Supporting both adds billing complexity. Which approach do you prioritize?

options.text: Pure usage-based for all segments to keep it simple
Hybrid: committed contracts for enterprise, usage-based for startups
Annual subscriptions only with tiered usage limits
Freemium for startups, custom enterprise pricing only

interactions.prompt: A fitness app is shifting from one-time purchase to subscription. Rank these actions from first to last for a successful transition.

options.text: Grandfather existing users on a discounted legacy plan
Build recurring content pipeline to justify ongoing subscription
Test subscription pricing with new user cohorts first
Announce full migration and sunset the one-time model

interactions.prompt: Your largest enterprise client (30% of ARR) now demands pure usage-based pricing or they'll leave. But your investors just praised your predictable subscription revenue. How do you respond?

options.text: Switch the whole company to usage-based pricing
Offer this client a hybrid: base commitment plus usage overages
Refuse and accept the risk of losing them
Give them usage-based pricing secretly with a custom contract

interactions.priorContext: Previously you chose a hybrid model supporting both enterprise contracts and startup usage-based pricing. Now your biggest client is pushing back against any committed spend, threatening your revenue concentration.
